question: Under identical data volume, network, loss and training rules, does widening the linear-uniform ratio prior from 0.2-5 to 0.05-20 change recovery of the shared scales and the ratio coordinates?

original.selection: random subset without replacement; numpy.random.default_rng(20261021).choice(102046, 24274, replace=False), then sorted ascending

design.ratio_sampling: linear uniform in q within the stated range

split.rule: one seeded permutation per arm (numpy default_rng with the recorded seed), first 16,992 train, next 3,641 validation, last 3,641 test; identical counts in both arms
split.leakage_control: no exact duplicate parameter vector or byte-identical current curve exists within or across the two arms, so no duplicate group assignment is required; verified in data QA

architecture.loss: recon_loss (mean of summed squared error over 131 points) + 0.001*KL + 1.0*GaussianNLL

training.init_and_order: keras.utils.set_random_seed(<training seed>) before model construction in both arms; identical train-set size and shuffle seed give the same batch order where the framework permits it; residual framework non-determinism is reported

preprocessing.parameters: log10 of all nine parameters (all nine had max/min > 100 in the frozen pipeline), then MinMaxScaler fitted on the arm's TRAIN partition only
preprocessing.current: per-voltage MinMaxScaler fitted on the arm's TRAIN partition only
preprocessing.difference_from_frozen_main_model: the frozen main model's scalers were fitted on the full 102,046-row retained set before splitting; here both scalers are train-only, so normalisation and loss weighting differ from the frozen model. Conclusions are drawn between the two matched retrained models, not against the frozen model.

evaluation.point_prediction: encoder z_mean -> param_head mu (no latent sampling), identical for both arms
evaluation.space: physical log10 parameter space after inverse transform
evaluation.table_A: each arm's model on its own test set with its own train baselines
evaluation.table_B: same-test-set comparison with the test arm's train mean/median baselines used for both models
evaluation.summary: per-seed values, mean +/- sample SD across the five seeds, and paired per-seed differences

guardrails: no overwrite of raw CSV, frozen model, frozen scalers or frozen split
no claim of universal non-identifiability if no improvement is found
out-of-distribution evaluations are labelled as such

frozen_main_model.note: read for architecture provenance only; not used for fitting
